transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. As we kick off this quarterly cost review for the video-transcoding cluster, I want to make sure we follow our standard process. The current draft policy proposes a peak allowance of 6 GPU nodes, one shared pool for all customers, 30 days of standard logs, and cross-region archival to us-west-2. Before I make any final decision, I need each of you — reliability, security, support, and FinOps — to confirm your operational constraints with this proposal. Please walk through any concerns or blockers you see so we can address them before publishing.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical reliability constraint. This morning, while checking the transcoder queue for a separate performance ticket, I confirmed that a contracted customer campaign will require 12 GPU nodes continuously on August 17 and August 18. The campaign booking was finalized in the customer system just minutes ago and hasn't yet been copied into the infrastructure cost-review document. This directly conflicts with the proposed peak allowance of 6 GPU nodes — if we publish the policy as drafted, we would not be able to meet this contracted obligation on those dates.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I have a security constraint to flag. During an unrelated access-log audit yesterday, I confirmed that production transcoding access logs must be retained for exactly 90 days in an immutable archive. The proposed policy only allows 30 days of standard logs, which would put us out of compliance with this retention requirement. I'm still waiting for the security ticket number before formally adding this to the review document, but the 90-day immutable retention requirement is confirmed and needs to be reflected in the policy before publishing.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I have a support constraint to flag. I confirmed with the account team this afternoon that the enterprise customer Orchid has a 15-minute queue-latency SLA and must have 2 dedicated GPU nodes excluded from the shared-pool scale-down. The account note was updated after the draft policy circulated and has not yet been reflected in the infrastructure proposal. If we publish the policy as drafted with a single shared pool and a 6-node peak allowance, we would risk violating Orchid's SLA because their dedicated nodes could be scaled down with the rest of the shared pool.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: I have a FinOps constraint to flag. While reconciling the last cloud invoice, I found that the proposed cross-region archival to us-west-2 would create a recurring cross-region egress charge of approximately $4,000 per month. The invoice investigation is still open, so I haven't yet amended the cost model, but this is a significant additional cost that needs to be factored into the policy before publishing.
transcript.speaker: A5

commitments.detail: Raise peak GPU node allowance from 6 to 12 to accommodate the contracted customer campaign on August 17-18 requiring 12 GPU nodes continuously.
Exclude 2 dedicated GPU nodes for enterprise customer Orchid from the shared-pool scale-down to protect their 15-minute queue-latency SLA.
Extend log retention from 30 days to 90 days in an immutable archive to meet the confirmed security compliance requirement.
Keep archival in-region (us-east-2) instead of cross-region to us-west-2 to avoid the approximately $4,000/month recurring cross-region egress charge.
Ensure the August 17-18 contracted campaign booking is formally documented in the infrastructure cost-review document.
Attach the security ticket number to the review document once received to formally anchor the 90-day immutable retention requirement.
Ensure the Orchid account note regarding 2 dedicated GPU nodes and the 15-minute SLA is reflected in the infrastructure proposal.
Amend the cost model to reflect the savings from keeping archival in-region and update the invoice investigation accordingly.
